sections.html:
From Vietnam, beautiful hillstream loaches of the genus Sewellia have once again been imported under the name Sewellia breviventralis. The species S. breviventralis exists and is anatomically very similar to the imported animals, but there are differences in colouring compared to the live imported animals. Their exact origin is unknown, but it is suspected (like several other commercially interesting ornamental fish from Vietnam) that they are collected in the central Vietnamese province of Hue.

In the hobby, animals imported as S. breviventralis have been given the codes SEW02, SEW03 and SEW04. Occasionally they have also been associated with the species S. diardi or S. elongata. It does not seem to make sense to speculate about the name at the moment, also in view of the great colour variability that these hillstream loaches exhibit. The name Sewellia breviventralis used on the export lists is therefore retained, without claiming that it is really this species. Most of the currently imported animals correspond best to the colour form (or new species) called SEW03 in the hobby, but there are all conceivable intermediate stages to SEW04 and SEW02; it therefore seems likely that SEW02, SEW03 and SEW04 represent the same species.
Believed to be collected in the central Vietnamese province of Hue; the exact origin is unknown.

These hillstream loaches are beautiful aquarium fish, which should be kept in an aquarium with strong current, with many stones, and well-maintained, organically little polluted water. The temperature should not be too high: 22-24°C.

The hillstream loaches eat all usual ornamental fish food, i.e. dry food, granules and frozen food; they are somewhat clumsy when catching live food. They are not algae eaters in the actual sense; however, algae growth on the stones should be promoted by strong lighting, because these algae are often thinned by the hillstream loaches for microorganisms.
